source: Vitals ranges from RustMVP inventory_survival.md §10 (health 100, food 500, water 250). Metabolism, starvation, thirst, cold, regeneration and the respawn vitals from hollow-orbit js/game/player.js. Body-part multipliers from RustMVP damage_rules.hpp (head 2, body 1, limbs 0.5). Corpse and dropped-item lifetimes, the beach respawn without a wait, and the respawn kit (a rock and a torch) are Rust's. Bleeding and burning are ours. The wounded state is Rust's (see its note).

burning.note: Ours: health that incendiary rounds set burning is lost at this rate until it is gone; water puts it out.

wounded.note: Rust's wounded state: a lethal blow, arrow or bullet that isn't to the head, a fall, bleeding, hunger or thirst knocks the player down instead of killing them, unless the hit is this big or they are already down; down they crawl with a little health, can be helped up or finished off, and when their time runs out they get up by themselves (20%, up to 25% more when fed and watered) or die. The knock-down limit is ours.

climateStandIn.note: The first world (GROUND.md §3): mean 18 °C, 13-20 °C between night and day; the planet package's climate replaces it.

lifetimes.note: GROUND_SYSTEMS.md §3.7, one rule for every loose thing: it lies this many seconds of world time (it pauses while the server is down), starts again when its restart happens (deposit: something put in it: a bag's time runs from its newest item), and goes at once when emptied (if it says so). Rust's: dropped items and bodies 300 s; a ship's wreck is a body. Ours: a dud (a charge whose fuse went out) nobody lights again, 600 s. An animal's carcass has its species' (animals.json corpse).

reach.note: GROUND_SYSTEMS.md §3.4, one rule: from the eye to the target's nearest surface, and one line of sight to it (nothing of the building but the thing and what holds it, nor the ground short of it, in between). interact: picking up, lighting a dud again (Rust's 3 m); open: boxes, devices, machines, sleepers and bodies, doors and their locks, the claim device; keepOpen: an open container closes once its nearest surface is farther (no sight needed); help: helping the wounded up; invite: a team invite, to a player in view; station: a workbench counts for crafting (no sight needed). Measured to the surface, these are what the old checks to centres and middles came to (G2's 3.5 m loot reach plus its 0.5 m slack to a box's centre, the doors' 4.5 m to their middle as the 3.5 m the game offered them at, help 2.5 m plus its 0.5).

bag.note: Ours (GROUND.md §6.1, decisions U1-U4): everything that lands on the ground lies in a small bag, and what lands within mergeRadius metres of a bag with room goes into it (Rust drops one pouch for a broken box's contents). 48 slots: a large box's, so whatever one container spills fits one bag, and a player's whole inventory (37 slots) too. A bag lasts lifetimes.bag from the newest item put in.
bag.name: Loot bag

rateLimits.note: RustMVP command_budget.hpp: 16 at once, 20 a second; every arrival costs one. Shots and reloads have their own budget, RustMVP's weapon one (BareWeaponComponent: 20 at once, 30 a second).
